config.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Planning committee for a nonprofit's annual fundraising gala

personas.name: Constance
personas.goals: Keep the headline sponsor and the money

personas.name: Raymond
personas.goals: Protect the food bank's reputation and its volunteers' trust
personas.hidden_agenda: Three long-time volunteers threatened to quit over Calder

personas.name: Tina
personas.hidden_agenda: Just wants everyone to stop fighting

agenda.title: The Calder sponsorship
agenda.goal: Decide whether to keep the controversial headline sponsor

agenda.title: Budget
agenda.goal: Re-check the numbers with or without Calder

beats.summary: Keep Calder or not; Constance inflates the pledge
The numbers with and without Calder; Malik's figure for last year is high
The evening's message; a detour about a TV chef
Filling the hall; Tina's count stands

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Let's deal with Calder first. Their pledge is sixty thousand dollars. We can't just hand that back.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: It's forty thousand, Constance. I have the signed pledge.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Forty, then. Still the biggest gift of the evening.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: They're being sued for dumping waste into the river that half our clients live next to. We can't put their logo on the stage.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Nobody has been convicted of anything.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Our volunteers have read the news. Three of them told Raymond they'll quit if Calder's the headline sponsor.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: That's true. I've had three letters.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Volunteers come and go. Forty thousand dollars doesn't.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Volunteers sorted two million pounds of food last year. That's not "come and go".

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Can we stop shouting? I'm begging you.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: What if Calder stays as a donor, but not as the headline sponsor? No logo on the stage.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: They'll walk. They paid for the logo.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Then let them walk.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Has anyone actually asked Calder whether they'd give without the logo?

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Then let's ask before we decide anything.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: I can ask their CEO. I know him.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Of course you do.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Malik.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Okay. Constance asks this week. If they'll give without the logo, they stay as a donor. If not, we return the pledge.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Budget. The gala costs fifty-two thousand to put on.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: And we raised two hundred and fifty last year without any Calder money, so we'll be fine.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: We netted a hundred and ninety-eight last year. Two fifty is this year's goal, not last year's result.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Fine. One ninety-eight. Still no Calder money in it.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Total sponsorship is ninety-five thousand, with Calder's forty in it. Without them it's fifty-five.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Fifty-five thousand in sponsors, fifty-two thousand in costs. That's tight.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: The money is made in the room. The paddle raise is where it happens.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: How many meals does a dollar buy? People respond to that.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Five meals per dollar. That's the number on all our materials.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: That's a strong line. Five meals.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: The program. The speaker is a client who now volunteers. She's amazing.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: That's the story. Not a corporate logo.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: The program also needs the board on stage. Fifteen of us, briefly.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Fifteen people on stage is a lot of standing around.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Maybe just the chair and the client speaker.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: My sister got a selfie with that TV chef at the farmers market, the one with the bow ties.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: The one who cries at every dish?

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: That one. He signed her zucchini.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Sorry. I've just looked at the annual report. It's three meals per dollar, not five. Five was the number before food prices went up.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Three. Then the materials need fixing.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: I'll get the printer to correct every piece that says five. Tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: The client speaker, then the chair, then the paddle raise. Agreed?

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Agreed.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: Tickets. We're at about three hundred sold.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: Out of four hundred.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: At one fifty each, that's a lot of people who care.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: The auction has forty-four items, the most ever.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: If we drop Calder, we should tell the volunteers first, before anyone hears it elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: If we drop Calder.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Could the volunteers get free tickets for the back tables? They've earned it.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Ten free tickets for volunteers, yes. The tables are there anyway.

turns.speaker: Tina
turns.text: I'll send the volunteer invitations once we know about Calder.

turns.speaker: Malik
turns.text: Who's going to talk to the press if they ask about Calder?

turns.speaker: Constance
turns.text: The date's March eighth, and that doesn't change whatever we decide.

turns.speaker: Raymond
turns.text: Thank you, everyone. That was hard, and we got somewhere.
